Step 2: Fill the form using accessibility-focused selectors. I prefer page.get_by_role("textbox", name=...) for text inputs and page.get_by_role("combobox", name=...) for selects. As a fallback, get_by_label is used where role-based selection may differ.
Step 3: For website and customer group checkboxes, I first try to target a group (page.get_by_role('group', name='Websites') / 'Customer Groups') and then iterate its checkboxes with .get_by_role('checkbox'). If that fails, I conservatively attempt to check a reasonable number of top-level checkboxes.
Step 4: Switch to the Actions tab using page.get_by_role('tab', name='Actions') and set the discount to 'Percent of product price discount' and discount amount to 45. I include a fallback to select by value 'by_percent' if the label selection fails.
Step 5: Save the rule by clicking an accessible button. Because this triggers navigation/submit, it is the final action. I try several possible visible button names and then wait for networkidle/load after clicking.
